title: Saudi Highway Code 203: Traffic Studies
claim: The Saudi code sets three peak-hour trip tiers: a circulation plan for 10 to under 100 trips, a traffic impact study above 100 and below 2,500 trips, and a traffic management plan above 2,500 trips; the authority may impose stricter requirements.
limitations: The thresholds govern development traffic studies; Masar should adapt them as explainable screening tiers for works rather than claim they are excavation-permit thresholds.
introducedChange: Adds a Saudi-code-aligned three-tier analysis mode.

title: Saudi Highway Code 203: Study Area and Capacity Tests
claim: The study area generally includes links and intersections where project traffic is at least 10% of total volume; access queue assessment is required when volume-to-capacity exceeds 0.5, and a value above 1.0 is unacceptable.
limitations: The 10% rule is written for proposed development traffic; for work zones Masar must label its use as an adopted influence-area rule pending authority validation.
introducedChange: Defines a defensible impact boundary and capacity flags.

title: Saudi Highway Code 203: Value of Travel Time
claim: The code values drive-alone commute time at 50% of hourly wage, carpool driver time at 60%, carpool passenger time at 40%, personal local travel at 50%, personal intercity travel at 70%, and business time at 100% of total compensation; it requires passenger occupancy rather than vehicle count alone.
limitations: A current wage and occupancy by vehicle class are still required; the code notes total compensation above wage and separate trucking treatment.
introducedChange: Replaces an unsupported flat riyal-per-hour assumption with an official Saudi formula.

title: Saudi Highway Code 203: Greenhouse-Gas External Cost Method
claim: The code instructs analysts to multiply vehicle-class emission factors by transport volume and provides urban peak, off-peak and rural greenhouse-gas external-cost factors by vehicle type.
limitations: The monetary table is expressed in 2005 Saudi riyals per vehicle-kilometre and must be updated before monetary use; Masar should present physical emissions first.
introducedChange: Adds a code-aligned emissions method and a mandatory price-year warning.

title: Saudi Highway Code 305: Smart Work Zone Technologies
claim: The code names traveler information, queue warning, variable speed limits, dynamic merging, construction-vehicle warnings, intrusion alarms, performance measurement, crowdsourcing integration, and WZDx for work-zone activity, worker presence and traffic-volume data.
limitations: The code identifies technologies and considerations; it does not prove that every Saudi authority currently operates them.
introducedChange: Makes a WZDx-compatible Saudi smart-work-zone layer a core differentiator.

title: Temporary Traffic Diversions: Review and Closeout
publisher: Ministry of Municipalities and Housing via the Public Consultation Platform
claim: The traffic-safety review period is capped at three working days, field monitoring must cover different times of day, and the final report records lessons learned, problems, solutions, risks and responses.
limitations: The source is hosted on the consultation platform; confirm final legal status with the authority before describing it as binding.
introducedChange: Supports an automated review dossier and a closed-loop learning record.

title: Temporary Traffic Diversion Plan Document Requirements
publisher: Ministry of Municipalities and Housing via the Public Consultation Platform
claim: The diversion-plan package includes WGS84 coordinates, a 1:1000 drawing, work area, traffic-control devices, closed movements and access arrangements, and is mandatory except for emergencies.
limitations: Confirm final legal status and any authority-specific template before production use.
introducedChange: Defines the fields Masar can prefill in a permit-review dossier.

title: Balady Excavation Interactive Map and Coordination Capabilities
claim: Balady already displays permitted excavation routes and supports filters for work status, utility service, excavation type, street closure, method and duration; future-project and multi-excavation coordination also exist.
limitations: Access can be permission-scoped; public evidence does not show pre-permit traffic prediction, quantified road-user cost, ranked schedules or post-work calibration.
introducedChange: Prevents the false claim that Masar is the first excavation map or first coordination layer.

title: Balady Open Data
claim: Balady publishes an open-data API and a data-request path with an indicated response within five working days.
limitations: The tested generic API did not expose an annual excavation-permit series; a targeted data request is still required.
introducedChange: Creates a formal acquisition path for the missing permit baseline.

title: Traffic Intersections by Main and Cross Street
publisher: Royal Commission for Riyadh City Open Data
claim: The machine-readable dataset contains 633 geocoded Riyadh traffic intersections.
limitations: The layer identifies intersections but does not itself provide current traffic volumes.
introducedChange: Supplies real local nodes for an honest prototype map.

title: Riyadh Public Transport and Air-Quality Open-Data Layers
publisher: Royal Commission for Riyadh City Open Data
claim: The catalog exposes 3,010 bus stops, 117 bus lines, 94 metro stations, 6 metro lines and 17 air-quality monitoring stations in machine-readable datasets.
limitations: Catalog counts and modification dates can change; snapshots should be refreshed before the final submission.
introducedChange: Adds transit-access and environmental receptors to the impact score.

title: RCRC Second Phase of the Main and Ring Road Development Program
claim: The second phase contains eight projects worth more than SAR 8 billion, includes corridors designed for 200,000 vehicles per day and Dirab Road at 340,000 vehicles per day, and is expected to run about three years.
limitations: These are planned post-development capacities, not observed work-zone traffic counts.
introducedChange: Provides a credible local scale narrative without inventing permit totals.

title: RCRC First Phase of the Main and Ring Road Development Program
claim: The first phase consists of four projects exceeding SAR 13 billion, covers large corridors over three to four years, and explicitly includes a coordinated traffic-diversion management plan.
limitations: The announcement does not publish project-level observed delays.
introducedChange: Identifies a strong Riyadh pilot portfolio and decision owner.

title: Road Transport Statistics 2024
claim: Saudi Arabia had 15.8 million registered roadworthy vehicles in 2024, up 6.9% from 2023; 17,231 serious traffic accidents were recorded and 60.3% occurred within cities.
limitations: National context cannot be attributed to excavation works and must not be used as Masar's claimed impact.
introducedChange: Adds official context while preserving causal discipline.

title: Livability in Saudi Cities 2025: Average Daily Commute
claim: Average daily round-trip commute time in Riyadh was 67 minutes in 2024, compared with 81 minutes in 2023 and 92 minutes in 2022.
limitations: The indicator covers commuting overall and does not isolate construction effects.
introducedChange: Creates an official resident-centered problem baseline.

title: Livability in Saudi Cities 2025: Urban Bus Passengers
claim: Riyadh urban bus passenger trips rose from 12 million in 2023 to more than 34.7 million in 2024.
limitations: This is annual ridership, not the number of passengers affected by a particular work zone.
introducedChange: Justifies weighting bus-route and stop disruption in the score.

title: Saudi Arabia Data Portal: Average Wage
claim: The average monthly wage per paid employee in the main job was SAR 5.8 thousand for the total population in the first quarter of 2026.
limitations: This national average is suitable only as a labeled demo parameter; production valuation should use trip-purpose and workforce-specific wages.
introducedChange: Enables an auditable demonstration of the Saudi code's time-value formula.

title: Riyadh Traffic Index 2025
claim: Riyadh's 2025 city view reports 43.7% average congestion, 90.4% evening-rush congestion, 24.8 km/h evening-rush speed and 66 hours lost per rush-hour driver.
limitations: The figures describe all congestion, not work-zone causality. The 28.5 km/h figure on the page is the combined rush-hour average, while 24.8 km/h is the evening-rush value.
introducedChange: Resolves the project's earlier apparent contradiction and restores the figures with the correct definitions.

title: Work Zone Data Exchange
claim: WZDx version 4.2 harmonizes work-zone, device and worker-presence data for third-party and in-vehicle use and is transitioning into a formal connected-work-zone standard.
limitations: It is a data specification, not a traffic-impact or optimization engine.
introducedChange: Defines Masar's outbound interoperability format.

title: Work Zone Road User Costs: Concepts and Applications
claim: Work-zone road-user cost comprises delay, vehicle operating, crash and emission costs; delay cost equals added personal, truck and freight-inventory time multiplied by unit values of time.
limitations: Unit costs must be localized; community and business impacts are often site-specific and should not be falsely monetized.
introducedChange: Defines a complete but conservative impact-accounting boundary.

title: Work Zone Safety and Mobility Performance Measures
claim: Recommended measures include queue frequency, duration and length, vehicle-hours of delay, per-vehicle delay, travel-time reliability, throughput, safety, customer complaints and agency productivity, with recurrent congestion separated from work-zone effects.
limitations: Thresholds must be set by the Saudi authority and local baseline conditions.
introducedChange: Turns Masar's impact page into a defensible measurement protocol.

title: Active Transportation and Demand Management in Work Zones
claim: An Illinois queue-warning deployment significantly reduced speed variance and vehicle conflicts and reduced queuing crashes by 14% despite greater lane closures and vehicle exposure.
limitations: This is an external precedent, not an Masar result and not directly transferable to Riyadh without a pilot.
introducedChange: Provides a labeled external validation target for the smart-work-zone module.

title: DATEX II
publisher: DATEX II and European CEN community
claim: DATEX II is the European reference standard for exchanging road traffic and travel information and includes roadworks, measured data, traffic management and machine-interpretable regulations.
limitations: Masar should prioritize WZDx for the prototype because the Saudi code names it, while keeping DATEX II as a future adapter.
introducedChange: Adds a standards roadmap beyond the prototype.

title: Causeway one.network Traffic Management
claim: The platform combines map-based work-zone and permit coordination, clash avoidance, public communication, WZDx feeds and direct integrations with major navigation applications.
limitations: Public product evidence does not show Saudi-code-aligned road-user-cost monetization or ranked permit-schedule optimization.
introducedChange: Establishes the strongest direct global benchmark.

title: PTV Vissim
claim: PTV Vissim performs microscopic multimodal simulation, scenario evaluation and analysis of congestion, emissions, intersections and network performance.
limitations: It is a specialist simulation tool, not a municipal excavation-permit and coordination workflow.
introducedChange: Defines an advanced-simulation integration tier rather than a product Masar should imitate.

title: Aimsun Live
claim: Aimsun Live is a real-time predictive traffic digital twin that uses live and historical data to forecast conditions in under five minutes and test traffic-management actions before intervention.
limitations: It does not publicly present a Saudi excavation-permit workflow or code-specific benefit-cost screen.
introducedChange: Sets the ceiling for Masar's future predictive engine and clarifies the prototype's lighter-weight scope.

title: Esri Road Closures
claim: Esri's solution maintains authoritative closures and detours, publishes them to residents and shares them with consumer mapping partners.
limitations: The cited solution is a communication and inventory layer, not predictive impact scoring or schedule optimization.
introducedChange: Defines a build-or-integrate option for the public map.

title: Major Roads Diversion Permit
claim: Dubai's electronic right-of-way service requires a detailed diversion layout and traffic-management and safety information and obliges contractors to coordinate reopening when congestion results.
limitations: The public page does not evidence pre-impact scoring, ranked timing alternatives or post-work model calibration.
introducedChange: Adds a regional permit-process comparator.

title: LTA PROMPT
claim: The portal handles street-work permits and road-closure notices; from October 2026 applicants on 30 identified roads must submit quarterly schedules at least two months in advance before permit approval.
limitations: The rule is specific to Singapore and takes effect after the research date.
introducedChange: Shows that future scheduling is becoming a permit prerequisite internationally.

title: Enhancement of Roadworks Application Process Using Artificial Intelligence
claim: Singapore reports about 200 to 300 roadworks daily and uses artificial intelligence to generate traffic-control plans, check documents with optical character recognition and recommend decisions for simpler applications.
limitations: This is a strong direct precedent; Masar must differentiate on network impact, quantified resident cost, schedule alternatives and learning after execution.
introducedChange: Raises the competitive bar and removes generic artificial-intelligence review as a unique claim.

title: Plan and Manage Roadworks
claim: Street Manager is mandatory for permits, assessments, inspections and reinstatements, publishes roadworks data through an API, and coordinates more than two million works each year.
limitations: It proves digital coordination at scale but not Masar's impact or a Saudi annual permit volume.
introducedChange: Refreshes an existing benchmark with the current official service definition.

title: NYC DOT Office of Construction Mitigation and Coordination
publisher: New York City Department of Transportation
claim: Selected street-work permits, including closures, primary arteries and Manhattan work, require review by the construction mitigation and coordination office before issuance.
limitations: The public evidence focuses on coordination and stipulations, not quantified predictive optimization.
introducedChange: Confirms a known governance precedent.

title: Qatar Permit Road Opening and Traffic Diversion Requirements
claim: Qatar's road-opening permit coordinates stakeholders and schedules, and a traffic-diversion plan is required for any job affecting traffic.
limitations: The source is a project manual and does not establish predictive impact scoring.
introducedChange: Adds a second Gulf workflow comparator.

title: TomTom Traffic API
claim: The API provides minute-updated observed speed, free-flow speed, travel time, quality indicators, incidents, delays, closures and roadworks.
limitations: Requires licensing and does not provide municipal permit decisions.
introducedChange: Defines a feasible premium data input for calibration.

title: INRIX Products
claim: INRIX offers real-time traffic monitoring, road and signal analytics, traffic counts, historic speeds and travel times, and origin-destination trip analytics.
limitations: Coverage and licensing for Riyadh must be confirmed; it is a data and analytics supplier rather than a permit optimizer.
introducedChange: Adds a second commercial calibration option.

title: StreetLight InSight Transportation Metrics
claim: StreetLight provides traffic counts, annual average daily traffic, origin-destination, turning movements, vehicle-kilometres or miles traveled, select-link and demographic analytics without deploying local sensors.
limitations: The cited coverage is North America, so it is a capability benchmark rather than a confirmed Riyadh input.
introducedChange: Adds a benchmark for affected-trip and equity analysis.

title: Safety Cloud for Construction and Work Zones
claim: The platform sends connected-vehicle and navigation alerts up to 30 seconds before work-zone hazards and records incident, trip, response and on-scene histories.
limitations: Performance claims on the product page require independent validation before reuse; this record relies only on evidenced capabilities.
introducedChange: Defines an optional field-safety integration, not a core permit feature.

title: Connected Arrow Boards and JamLogic
claim: Connected arrow boards and portable sensors publish lane-closure status, speed and device data to management software and WZDx-compatible feeds for navigation and traffic systems.
limitations: Hardware availability, certification, communications and climate suitability in Saudi Arabia require procurement validation.
introducedChange: Defines a later sensor-backed calibration path.

title: Trimble Cityworks Right-of-Way Permitting
claim: The GIS-centric workflow digitizes right-of-way permit submission, review, inspection, public access and spatial location management.
limitations: A vendor case study is weaker than independent evaluation and does not evidence predictive mobility impact.
introducedChange: Adds a permitting-workflow benchmark.

title: Environmental Impacts from Traffic on Highway Construction Work Zones
claim: The study develops a simulation framework for estimating vehicle fuel use and environmental impacts caused by highway construction work-zone closure conditions.
limitations: Model scenarios are not Saudi observations; local fleet, fuel, temperature and traffic inputs are required.
introducedChange: Supports measuring emissions from the traffic effect of works rather than only construction materials.
